name: postgres-mcp
purpose: PostgreSQL query access and performance analysis for agents
description: Postgres MCP Pro (crystaldba): configurable read/write SQL access, schema inspection and performance/tuning analysis for PostgreSQL. Successor to the archived @modelcontextprotocol/server-postgres reference server.
install_command: uvx postgres-mcp  (alternatives: pipx install postgres-mcp | docker pull crystaldba/postgres-mcp)
connect_steps: Add to config.yaml: mcp_servers.postgres-mcp = {command: uvx, args: [postgres-mcp]} (or: hermes mcp add postgres-mcp -- uvx postgres-mcp)
Set env POSTGRES_CONNECTION_STRING=postgres://user:pass@host:5432/db (or POSTGRES_DSN) in the server's env block / .env
Restart Hermes; verify tools appear as mcp__postgres-mcp__* via hermes mcp list

name: mysql-mcp-server
purpose: Secure MySQL database access (read/write queries + schema)
description: Most-starred MySQL MCP server: natural-language SQL against MySQL with schema inspection, query execution and safety controls. Env-driven config (no command-line secrets).
connect_steps: Add to config.yaml: mcp_servers.mysql-mcp-server = {command: uvx, args: [mysql_mcp_server]}
Set env MYSQL_HOST, MYSQL_PORT, MYSQL_USER, MYSQL_PASSWORD, MYSQL_DATABASE
Restart Hermes; verify mcp__mysql-mcp-server__* tools via hermes mcp list

name: sqlite-mcp
purpose: SQLite database access for local .db files
description: Lightweight SQLite MCP server (npm/bun ecosystem, egoist) — create, query and manage local SQLite databases. Zero-config for file-based dev workflows.
connect_steps: Add to config.yaml: mcp_servers.sqlite-mcp = {command: npx, args: [-y, sqlite-mcp, /path/to/dev.db]}
Point the DB path argument at your SQLite file (created if missing)
Restart Hermes; verify mcp__sqlite-mcp__* tools via hermes mcp list

name: mongodb-mcp-server
purpose: MongoDB and MongoDB Atlas data access
description: Official MongoDB MCP server: query, analyze and manage MongoDB databases and Atlas clusters. Supports read-only mode, stdio and HTTP transports.
install_command: npx -y mongodb-mcp-server@latest  (also: docker run --rm -i -e MONGODB_URI=... mongodb/mongodb-mcp-server)
connect_steps: Add to config.yaml: mcp_servers.mongodb-mcp-server = {command: npx, args: [-y, mongodb-mcp-server@latest]}
Set env MONGODB_URI=mongodb://user:pass@host:27017 (or Atlas connection string); add --readOnly to forbid writes
Restart Hermes; verify mcp__mongodb-mcp-server__* tools via hermes mcp list

name: redis-mcp-server
purpose: Redis data management and search for agents
description: Official Redis MCP server: natural-language interface to manage and search Redis data (keys, hashes, streams, vector/RediSearch queries).
install_command: uvx redis-mcp-server --url redis://localhost:6379/0  (alternatives: pip install redis-mcp-server | uvx --from git+https://github.com/redis/mcp-redis.git redis-mcp-server)
connect_steps: Add to config.yaml: mcp_servers.redis-mcp-server = {command: uvx, args: [redis-mcp-server, --url, redis://localhost:6379/0]}
Set REDIS_URL (or --url) to your instance; add --password / --username if auth is enabled
Restart Hermes; verify mcp__redis-mcp-server__* tools via hermes mcp list

name: mcp-server-motherduck
purpose: DuckDB (local) and MotherDuck (cloud) analytics
description: Official MotherDuck MCP server for DuckDB: local :memory:/file databases plus MotherDuck cloud analytics (md:). Full read/write SQL with database switching.
connect_steps: Add to config.yaml: mcp_servers.duckdb = {command: uvx, args: [mcp-server-motherduck, --db-path, :memory:, --read-write]}
Local: no env needed. MotherDuck cloud: set env motherduck_token=<token> and use --db-path md:
Restart Hermes; verify mcp__duckdb__* tools via hermes mcp list

name: snowflake-labs-mcp
purpose: Snowflake SQL, object management and Cortex AI
description: Official Snowflake MCP server: SQL orchestration, object management, semantic view consumption and Cortex AI features. Configured via a service-config YAML.
connect_steps: Add to config.yaml: mcp_servers.snowflake = {command: uvx, args: [snowflake-labs-mcp, --service-config-file, config.yaml]}
Create config.yaml with account/user/password (or keypair) + role/warehouse/database settings
Restart Hermes; verify mcp__snowflake__* tools via hermes mcp list

name: mcp-server-bigquery
purpose: Google BigQuery schema inspection and SQL execution
description: Google-published BigQuery MCP server: lets LLMs inspect database schemas and execute queries on BigQuery datasets (PyPI mcp-server-bigquery).
connect_steps: Add to config.yaml: mcp_servers.bigquery = {command: uvx, args: [mcp-server-bigquery]}
Set env GOOGLE_APPLICATION_CREDENTIALS=/path/to/service-account.json (or run gcloud auth application-default login)
Restart Hermes; verify mcp__bigquery__* tools via hermes mcp list

name: mcp-clickhouse
purpose: ClickHouse SQL analytics access
description: Official ClickHouse MCP server: connect ClickHouse to AI assistants for natural-language SQL analytics over ClickHouse clusters (incl. chdb embedded mode).
connect_steps: Add to config.yaml: mcp_servers.clickhouse = {command: python3, args: [-m, mcp_clickhouse]} (after pip install)
Set env CLICKHOUSE_HOST, CLICKHOUSE_PORT, CLICKHOUSE_USER, CLICKHOUSE_PASSWORD, CLICKHOUSE_DATABASE
Restart Hermes; verify mcp__clickhouse__* tools via hermes mcp list

name: supabase-mcp
purpose: Supabase Postgres, Auth, Storage and Edge Functions
description: Official Supabase MCP server: manage projects, run SQL against Postgres, and use Auth/Storage/Edge Function tools. Hosted at mcp.supabase.com (OAuth login) or self-hosted via Docker.
install_command: Remote HTTP server - config url https://mcp.supabase.com/mcp (self-host: docker run supabase/mcp-server)
connect_steps: Add to config.yaml: mcp_servers.supabase = {type: http, url: https://mcp.supabase.com/mcp}
Log in with your Supabase account when prompted (OAuth); select target organization/project
Restart Hermes; verify mcp__supabase__* tools via hermes mcp list

name: neon-mcp-server
purpose: Neon Postgres management and SQL (serverless Postgres)
description: Official Neon MCP server: manage Neon projects/branches and run SQL against serverless Postgres via the hosted endpoint mcp.neon.tech.
install_command: Remote HTTP server - https://mcp.neon.tech/mcp (npx add-mcp https://mcp.neon.tech/mcp)
connect_steps: Add to config.yaml: mcp_servers.neon = {type: http, url: https://mcp.neon.tech/mcp}
Set Authorization header / env NEON_API_KEY from console.neon.tech
Restart Hermes; verify mcp__neon__* tools via hermes mcp list

name: elasticsearch-mcp-server
purpose: Elasticsearch search and document operations
description: Official Elastic MCP server: run queries, inspect indices and manage documents in Elasticsearch (self-managed or Elastic Cloud).
install_command: docker run -i --rm -e ES_URL -e ES_API_KEY docker.elastic.co/mcp/elasticsearch stdio
connect_steps: Add to config.yaml: mcp_servers.elasticsearch = {command: docker, args: [run, -i, --rm, -e, ES_URL, -e, ES_API_KEY, docker.elastic.co/mcp/elasticsearch, stdio]}
Set env ES_URL=https://mycluster:9200 and ES_API_KEY (or ES_USERNAME/ES_PASSWORD)
Restart Hermes; verify mcp__elasticsearch__* tools via hermes mcp list

name: chroma-mcp
purpose: Chroma vector database collections and retrieval
description: Official Chroma MCP server: create collections, upsert embeddings and retrieve context from the open-source Chroma vector database (local or Chroma Cloud).
connect_steps: Add to config.yaml: mcp_servers.chroma = {command: uvx, args: [chroma-mcp, --path, ./chroma]}
Local: point --path at the Chroma dir (default ./chroma). Cloud: set CHROMA_HOST/CHROMA_PORT/CHROMA_SSL/CHROMA_AUTH_TOKEN
Restart Hermes; verify mcp__chroma__* tools via hermes mcp list

name: mcp-server-qdrant
purpose: Qdrant vector database search and collections
description: Official Qdrant MCP server: hybrid/vector search, collection management and point upserts against Qdrant (local, Docker or Qdrant Cloud).
connect_steps: Add to config.yaml: mcp_servers.qdrant = {command: uvx, args: [mcp-server-qdrant]}
Set env QDRANT_URL=http://localhost:6333 and QDRANT_API_KEY (if cloud/authenticated)
Restart Hermes; verify mcp__qdrant__* tools via hermes mcp list

name: weaviate-mcp-builtin
purpose: Weaviate vector DB hybrid search and collections
description: Weaviate MCP server is now BUILT INTO the main weaviate/weaviate binary (v1.37.1+): no separate install — enable with MCP_SERVER_ENABLED=true, served at /v1/mcp on the REST port (standalone weaviate/mcp-server-weaviate repo is deprecated).
install_command: No install - built into weaviate/weaviate v1.37.1+: run weaviate with MCP_SERVER_ENABLED=true (endpoint http://host:8080/v1/mcp)
connect_steps: Start Weaviate with env MCP_SERVER_ENABLED=true (v1.37.1+); endpoint is http://<host>:8080/v1/mcp
Add to config.yaml: mcp_servers.weaviate = {type: http, url: http://localhost:8080/v1/mcp}; set WEAVIATE_API_KEY if auth/RBAC enabled
Restart Hermes; verify mcp__weaviate__* tools (hybrid query, collections, upsert) via hermes mcp list

name: mcp-server-milvus
purpose: Milvus vector database operations
description: Official Zilliz Milvus MCP server: collections, embeddings and vector search against Milvus/Zilliz Cloud. Run via uv from the repo (Python 3.10+, uv).
install_command: git clone https://github.com/zilliztech/mcp-server-milvus.git && cd mcp-server-milvus && uv run src/mcp_server_milvus/server.py --milvus-uri http://localhost:19530
connect_steps: Clone repo and run server via uv (command above); add to config.yaml: mcp_servers.milvus = {command: uv, args: [run, .../server.py, --milvus-uri, http://localhost:19530]}
Set --milvus-uri / --milvus-token (or .env MILVUS_URI) for Zilliz Cloud
Restart Hermes; verify mcp__milvus__* tools via hermes mcp list

name: pinecone-mcp
purpose: Pinecone vector index upsert, search and config
description: Official Pinecone Developer MCP server: search docs, configure indexes, and upsert/search vectors in Pinecone projects (npm @pinecone-database/mcp).
connect_steps: Add to config.yaml: mcp_servers.pinecone = {command: npx, args: [-y, @pinecone-database/mcp]}
Set env PINECONE_API_KEY (generate in console.pinecone.io); optionally PINECONE_INDEX_NAME
Restart Hermes; verify mcp__pinecone__* tools via hermes mcp list

name: mcp-neo4j
purpose: Neo4j graph database queries and knowledge-graph memory
description: Official Neo4j MCP server: natural-language Cypher queries, graph data modeling and knowledge-graph memory against Neo4j or Aura (pip neo4j-mcp-server).
install_command: pip install neo4j-mcp-server  (server package; config via MCP settings)
connect_steps: pip install neo4j-mcp-server; add to config.yaml: mcp_servers.neo4j = {command: <venv>/python, args: [-m, neo4j_mcp_server]}
Set env NEO4J_URI=bolt://localhost:7687, NEO4J_USERNAME, NEO4J_PASSWORD (Aura: neo4j+s://... + Aura creds)
Restart Hermes; verify mcp__neo4j__* tools via hermes mcp list

name: prisma-mcp
purpose: Prisma ORM schema and database operations
description: Official Prisma MCP server: inspect Prisma schema, run migrations and query databases managed by Prisma ORM (local: npx prisma mcp; hosted: mcp.prisma.io).
install_command: npx -y prisma mcp  (remote: npx -y mcp-remote https://mcp.prisma.io/mcp)
connect_steps: Add to config.yaml: mcp_servers.prisma = {command: npx, args: [-y, prisma, mcp]} (run from your Prisma project dir)
Set env DATABASE_URL for the target database (as in your .env/prisma schema)
Restart Hermes; verify mcp__prisma__* tools via hermes mcp list

name: aws-dynamodb-mcp-server
purpose: AWS DynamoDB table operations and queries
description: Official AWS Labs MCP server (awslabs/mcp monorepo): full DynamoDB tooling — list/describe tables, get/put/query/scan items — via boto3 (PyPI awslabs.dynamodb-mcp-server).
connect_steps: Add to config.yaml: mcp_servers.aws-dynamodb = {command: uvx, args: [awslabs.dynamodb-mcp-server@latest]}
Set env AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID, AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY, AWS_REGION (or rely on ~/.aws credentials)
Restart Hermes; verify mcp__aws-dynamodb__* tools via hermes mcp list

name: aws-redshift-mcp-server
purpose: AWS Redshift SQL queries and cluster metadata
description: Official AWS Labs MCP server (awslabs/mcp monorepo): run SQL against Redshift warehouses and inspect cluster/database metadata via boto3 (PyPI awslabs.redshift-mcp-server).
connect_steps: Add to config.yaml: mcp_servers.aws-redshift = {command: uvx, args: [awslabs.redshift-mcp-server@latest]}
Set env AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID, AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY, AWS_REGION and Redshift connection details (cluster id/db/user)
Restart Hermes; verify mcp__aws-redshift__* tools via hermes mcp list

name: aws-api-mcp-server
purpose: Broad AWS API access (EC2, S3, Lambda, IAM, ...) via boto3
description: Official AWS Labs main MCP server (awslabs/mcp monorepo): general-purpose boto3-powered tool access across AWS services — EC2, S3, Lambda, IAM, CloudWatch and more (PyPI awslabs.aws-api-mcp-server).
connect_steps: Add to config.yaml: mcp_servers.aws-api = {command: uvx, args: [awslabs.aws-api-mcp-server@latest]}
Set env AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID, AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY, AWS_REGION (or default credential chain)
Restart Hermes; verify mcp__aws-api__* tools via hermes mcp list

name: aws-iac-mcp-server
purpose: AWS infrastructure-as-code (CloudFormation validation)
description: Official AWS Labs IaC MCP server (awslabs/mcp monorepo): validates and generates CloudFormation templates, translates CDK/CloudFormation and documents IaC resources.
connect_steps: Add to config.yaml: mcp_servers.aws-iac = {command: uvx, args: [awslabs.aws-iac-mcp-server@latest]}
Set env AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID, AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY, AWS_REGION for template validation
Restart Hermes; verify mcp__aws-iac__* tools via hermes mcp list

name: azure-mcp-server
purpose: Azure resource management and operations
description: Official Microsoft Azure MCP server (microsoft/mcp monorepo, successor to archived Azure/azure-mcp): manage Azure resources, run Azure CLI operations and query subscriptions. .NET-based, npm/dotnet install.
install_command: npx -y @azure/mcp@latest server start  (alternatives: npm install -g @azure/mcp | dotnet tool install Azure.Mcp)
connect_steps: Add to config.yaml: mcp_servers.azure = {command: npx, args: [-y, @azure/mcp@latest, server, start]}
Authenticate: az login, or set env AZURE_TENANT_ID, AZURE_CLIENT_ID, AZURE_CLIENT_SECRET, AZURE_SUBSCRIPTION_ID
Restart Hermes; verify mcp__azure__* tools via hermes mcp list

name: mcp-server-kubernetes
purpose: Kubernetes cluster management via kubectl
description: Most-starred Kubernetes MCP server (Flux159): inspect and manage pods, deployments, services, namespaces and cluster state through kubectl (npm mcp-server-kubernetes).
connect_steps: Add to config.yaml: mcp_servers.kubernetes = {command: npx, args: [mcp-server-kubernetes]}
Set env KUBECONFIG=/path/to/kubeconfig (or rely on in-cluster config); kubectl must be on PATH
Restart Hermes; verify mcp__kubernetes__* tools via hermes mcp list

name: terraform-mcp-server
purpose: Terraform plan/apply/validate automation
description: Official HashiCorp Terraform MCP server: validate, plan and apply Terraform configurations, inspect state and resources from the agent. Docker or Go binary install.
install_command: docker run -i --rm hashicorp/terraform-mcp-server  (alternatives: go install github.com/hashicorp/terraform-mcp-server/cmd/terraform-mcp-server@latest | brew install terraform-mcp-server)
connect_steps: Add to config.yaml: mcp_servers.terraform = {command: docker, args: [run, -i, --rm, hashicorp/terraform-mcp-server]}
Mount your Terraform workspace: add -v $(pwd):/workspace and set TF_WORKSPACE_DIR=/workspace
Restart Hermes; verify mcp__terraform__* tools via hermes mcp list

name: docker-mcp-gateway
purpose: Docker container and MCP server lifecycle management
description: Official Docker MCP plugin + Gateway (docker/docker-mcp, formerly mcp-gateway): run/manage Docker containers and securely host MCP servers from the Docker MCP Catalog (npx/uvx/docker entries) behind one gateway.
install_command: Docker Desktop 4.59+ MCP Toolkit (docker mcp CLI bundled); or git clone https://github.com/docker/mcp-gateway && make docker-mcp
connect_steps: Enable MCP Toolkit in Docker Desktop 4.59+ (or build the CLI plugin: git clone + make docker-mcp)
Run 'docker mcp catalog pull mcp/docker-mcp-catalog' then 'docker mcp profile create --name dev-tools --server catalog://mcp/docker-mcp-catalog/github --connect hermes'
Restart Hermes; verify mcp__docker__* tools via hermes mcp list

name: mcp-server-cloudflare
purpose: Cloudflare account, Workers, DNS, KV/R2 management
description: Official Cloudflare MCP server (npm @cloudflare/mcp-server-cloudflare): manage Workers, DNS, KV, R2, Pages and account settings through typed domain-specific tools.
connect_steps: Add to config.yaml: mcp_servers.cloudflare = {command: npx, args: [-y, @cloudflare/mcp-server-cloudflare]}
Set env CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN with the right permissions (or CLOUDFLARE_API_KEY + CLOUDFLARE_EMAIL); optional CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID
Restart Hermes; verify mcp__cloudflare__* tools via hermes mcp list

name: workers-mcp
purpose: Expose your own Cloudflare Worker as an MCP server
description: Official Cloudflare tool: turns any Cloudflare Worker into an MCP server so agents can call your deployed Worker functions (npm workers-mcp).
connect_steps: Run 'npx workers-mcp setup' in a Workers project (or create one: npx create-cloudflare@latest)
Follow the interactive login + worker selection; it wires the client config automatically
Verify tools from your Worker appear as mcp__* in Hermes via hermes mcp list

name: cloudflare-mcp-code-mode
purpose: Cloudflare API via hosted code-mode server
description: Official Cloudflare Code Mode MCP server (cloudflare/mcp): broad Cloudflare API coverage through code execution, hosted at mcp.cloudflare.com — complements the domain-specific servers.
install_command: Remote HTTP server - url https://mcp.cloudflare.com/mcp (code mode)
connect_steps: Add to config.yaml: mcp_servers.cloudflare-code = {type: http, url: https://mcp.cloudflare.com/mcp}
Authenticate with CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN (account scoped) via header/bearer
Restart Hermes; verify mcp__cloudflare-code__* tools via hermes mcp list

name: netlify-mcp
purpose: Netlify deploys, sites, env vars and forms
description: Official Netlify MCP server (npm @netlify/mcp): create/manage projects, trigger deploys, manage env vars, forms and team info. Node.js 22+ required.
connect_steps: Add to config.yaml: mcp_servers.netlify = {command: npx, args: [-y, @netlify/mcp]} (Node 22+ required)
Set env NETLIFY_PERSONAL_ACCESS_TOKEN (PAT from app.netlify.com user settings > OAuth) or log in via netlify-cli
Restart Hermes; verify mcp__netlify__* tools via hermes mcp list

name: aap-mcp-server
purpose: Red Hat Ansible Automation Platform job automation
description: Official Red Hat Ansible MCP server (ansible/aap-mcp-server): run and monitor Ansible Automation Platform jobs, inventories and templates from the agent.
install_command: git clone https://github.com/ansible/aap-mcp-server.git && cd aap-mcp-server && npm install (then build/run per server subdir)
connect_steps: Clone repo and npm install (README instructions); add to config.yaml: mcp_servers.ansible = {command: node, args: [.../dist/server.js]}
Set env for AAP connection: AAP_HOST, AAP_TOKEN (or username/password) for your Automation Platform controller
Restart Hermes; verify mcp__ansible__* tools via hermes mcp list
